summary: Round-2 adversarial re-verify of the 5 heals + re-sweep heal-adjacent systems for NEW P0/P1

heal_verdicts.reasoning:
VERIFY (a) — PARITY HOLDS. The not-found branch (file:line 59-77) now executes `Hash::check((string)$request->post('password'), '$2y$12$iCTCxFekHaX...')` UNCONDITIONALLY at line 69-72 before the 400 return at line 74. There is no early return between the `if (!$kioskMachine)` entry and the Hash::check, so it always pays the bcrypt cost. The found-but-wrong-password branch (line 86) runs exactly one `Hash::check($password, $kioskMachine->password)`. Both paths therefore perform a single bcrypt verification at the same configured cost. Measured: both the placeholder and a real cost-12 hash verify in ~360-391ms (avg 391ms over 5 runs), which dwarfs the sub-millisecond DB-row-fetch delta between a successful vs failed `where('username',...)->first()`. The bcrypt computation dominates total latency, so found vs not-found are no longer distinguishable by timing. Both return the same generic 'credentials_invalid' 400 (F3 message-parity, line 75 vs line 88) — message + latency parity both hold.

VERIFY (b) — NO RESIDUAL USERNAME-ENUMERATION ORACLE. Two earlier returns skip bcrypt: (1) validator fail at line 35-39 (422) fires only on malformed input (missing/empty/min:6 violation) — syntactic, independent of whether the username exists in the DB; (2) the `str_contains($username, '@')` gate at line 42-46 (422) returns at ~0ms with no Hash::check. Critically, NEITHER is an existence oracle: a real registered username and a fake one — both well-formed and both lacking '@' — flow identically past these gates into the bcrypt-paid paths. An attacker enumerating valid usernames cannot use the '@' gate to distinguish real from fake accounts (it only reflects a syntactic property of the string they themselves supplied). So no timing distinguisher remains for the enumeration threat the heal targets. (Minor: a stored null/empty machine password would make Hash::check on the found path short-circuit fast, but the not-found placeholder always pays full cost, so the not-found path is never cheaper than found — the conservative/safe direction — and empty machine passwords are a data-state edge, not a normal enumeration vector.)

VERIFY (c) — PLACEHOLDER VALID AT CONFIGURED COST. password_get_info on '$2y$12$iCTCxFekHaXKl6P5xGvk6eZOWy6HTwGk6DCXW5xj8MuK104fpZh2W' returns algoName=bcrypt, options.cost=12. config/hashing.php:39 sets bcrypt rounds to env('BCRYPT_ROUNDS', 12). The placeholder cost (12) matches the configured cost, so the not-found path pays the SAME number of bcrypt rounds the found path pays for any normally-hashed machine password.

DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH CONTEXT: routes/api.php:167-168 wraps /kiosk-login in middleware('throttle:kiosk-login') (30/min per the iter15 D-001 limiter), so statistical timing attacks needing thousands of samples are throttled. V1-LOCAL fence (single-box, 1 branch) makes this low-severity regardless; the heal is cloud-ready defense-in-depth. No frozen zone touched.

The heal at KitchenDisplaySystemOrderService.php:600-606 is logically correct and well-targeted. Empirical execution of the exact normalize logic confirms: (a) double-encoded JSON-string-of-array unwraps to the real codes and produces a hash identical to the correctly-encoded twin (items merge, food-safe); (b) triple-encode/null/scalar collapse to [] — acceptable because no current write path produces triple-encode (all persist via OrderItem::insert() which bypasses the 'array' cast = single-encode, or OrderItem::create() reading-through-then-writing-through the cast = single-encode) and [] is the regression-safe merge default. The double-encoded shape is a REAL legacy artifact, not theoretical: migration 2026_05_20_120000:97-98 explicitly cleans '"[]"' and BackfillAllergensSnapshotTest.php:72 references the double-encode-on-create risk; that migration only cleans KDS-visible OPEN orders, leaving immutable closed-order rows potentially double-encoded. The heal commit 41d1e8ba7 ships a matching TDD sentinel (KdsAllergenAggregationSplitTest.php:246 test_double_encoded_allergens_snapshot_merges_with_correctly_encoded). BUT (c) the fix is hash-only. The two other allergen read paths the prompt named are NOT hardened: KDSOrderItemsResource.php:39 safeJsonDecodeArray returns [] on a double-encoded value (FrontendOrderService.php:1114-1120 / the resource's own safeJsonDecodeArray do a single json_decode only — empirically returns []), so the items-board endpoint exposes zero codes; and kdsCustomization.js:152 keys off Array.isArray and therefore renders no allergen block for that [] payload. So on a double-encoded row the split/merge is now correct, yet the chef's actual displayed allergen list is still empty — the displayed-allergen leg of the same food-safety risk remains open. Live DB confirmation was not possible: the worktree .env points at the operating 'foodking' DB (which lacks the allergens_snapshot column) not the :8780 isolated foodking_2dot0, and the read-only fence forbids probing; this does not change the code-level verdict.

Sub-question verdicts:

(a) CAN A RUPTURED ITEM STILL BE SOLD ANOTHER WAY? YES — confirmed.
- /api/admin/item/details/{item} (routes/api.php:731 -> ItemController::itemDetails, lines 226-247) gates only on isVisibleOn($surface) (channel visibility), never on ItemBranchAvailability. The backing service ItemService::itemDetails (ItemService.php:674-677) just does $item->load(...) with NO branch-availability overlay. The overlay applyBranchAvailabilityOverlay is wired ONLY into simpleList (ItemService.php:123), not into itemDetails or show. Live-confirmed against foodking_2dot0 as POS operator (pos@lecayenne.fr, branch=1, can_pos=1, can_items_show=0): the details route resolves by channel alone (item 12 Cheddar = pos-sellable returns based on category channel; item 2 = admin-only category returns 404 by channel, not by rupture).
- The order-creation SSOT PricingService::calculateOrder (PricingService.php:119-320, frozen) validates top-level item EXISTENCE (lines 127-133) and addon/choice is_available (lines 531, 646) but NEVER checks ItemBranchAvailability for the top-level item, and does not even check the global $dbItem->is_available for it.
- grep confirms zero ItemBranchAvailability references in OrderService.php, PosController.php, PosOrderController.php. POST /api/admin/pos (routes/api.php:817 -> PosController::store -> OrderService -> PricingService) therefore prices and bills a ruptured item submitted by id. Net: operator fetches the ruptured item via /details/{id}?surface=pos (200), adds it to cart by item_id, submits the order, and it is charged. Rupture is still sellable.

(b) ADMIN PATH STILL 200? YES — correct. forcePosRuntimeBranchScope (ItemController.php:312-326) returns null when the user has items_show (admins do, line 315), so the new rupture block (lines 281-293) is skipped; admin/branch_id=0 barcode lookup resolves normally.

(c) BRANCH RESOLVED SERVER-SIDE (NOT CLIENT-FORGEABLE)? YES — correct. forcePosRuntimeBranchScope reads (int) $user->branch_id from the authenticated user (line 319), aborts 403 if <1 (line 320). Not derived from any client param. Live-confirmed branch=1 resolved from auth.

CONCLUSION: The heal does exactly what it claims at the barcode route and is itself robust, but rupture enforcement is point-fixed at one of three entry points. The same ruptured SKU is reachable (details-by-id) and sellable (order create) with no rupture validation, defeating the heal's stated intent (prevent selling a ruptured item). Severity P1: real money loss / NF525 mismatch (operator can bill a SKU the branch dashboard flags RUPTURE), within V1-LOCAL single-box scope, not a cloud/multi-tenant concern.

HEAL #12 (DashboardService::topItemsOfDay now uses ->realizedRevenue() instead of where(payment_status=PAID)) is verified correct on all four sub-questions.

(a) Does the RETURNED/REFUNDED negative-qty mirror now net the refunded units? YES. RefundWithCounterEntryService creates the mirror's OrderItem rows with quantity = -1 * item->quantity (RefundWithCounterEntryService.php:154) and total_price = -1 * item->total_price (:166). topItemsOfDay does SUM(quantity) AS qty_sum and SUM(total_price) AS revenue_sum (DashboardService.php:851-852) over OrderItems whose order passes realizedRevenue(). Since the mirror order is now included (see b), its negative-qty/negative-revenue items are summed in, netting the refunded units and revenue out. Pre-heal the filter was payment_status=PAID, and the mirror's payment_status=REFUNDED (RefundWithCounterEntryService.php:114), so the mirror was dropped and the parent kept its full sold qty — the exact bug the comment at DashboardService.php:854-859 describes.

(b) Does realizedRevenue() include both mirror and original paid parent? YES, and exactly once each. scopeRealizedRevenue (Order.php:296-307) is an OR of two disjoint branches: (1) payment_status=PAID AND status NOT IN (CANCELED,REJECTED,RETURNED) — matches the parent; (2) status=RETURNED AND parent_order_id NOT NULL — matches only the mirror. Confirmed the parent is never mutated by the refund: RefundWithCounterEntryService creates a NEW Order (Order::create at :108) and the only parent->status reference is a read-guard at :86 (grep for parent->save/update/status found nothing else). So the parent stays PAID/non-RETURNED (paid branch) and the mirror is RETURNED+parent_order_id (mirror branch) — both included, no overlap.

(c) Double-count or sign error? NONE. The two scope branches are mutually exclusive (a RETURNED+parent mirror cannot satisfy the paid branch's whereNotIn status). Signs are consistent: parent items +qty/+total_price, mirror items -qty/-total_price, so the GROUP BY item_id SUMs net toward the true sold quantity. revenue_sum nets the same way. orderByDesc(qty_sum) on netted qty is the intended ranking.

(d) Are siblings consistent? Within the statisticsForDay() widget that calls topItemsOfDay (DashboardService.php:704), #12 makes top_items consistent with total_ca/total_tva, which already use the net realized set (:692-693, isRealizedRevenueRow at :685-688). The other DASH-NET money surfaces are ALSO already netted: orderStatistics total_sales (:233-238 realizedRevenue), totalSales (:370), per-day chart (:258). The prompt's claim that OrderService:2974 (sales-report total_discounts) is un-netted is FALSE — that block filters via isRealizedRevenueRow at OrderService.php:2971 and money figures use $paidOrders (the netted set) at :2973-2975, with an explicit SALES-NET-01 comment (:2966-2970) stating parity with the dashboard scope. The ONE genuinely un-netted sibling is customerStates() hourly chart (:316-322), which ->count()s all orders incl. mirrors — but that is a customer-volume chart outside #12's scope and was already inconsistent before this heal, so #12 did not introduce or worsen it.

HEAL VERIFIED CORRECT AND COMPLETE.

(a) Uppercase customer declared allergen vs lowercase item code FIRES the red role=alert. collisionSet (KsAllergenBadge.vue:112) lowercases customer codes: new Set(customerAllergens.map(c => String(c).toLowerCase())). hasCollision (lines 114-116) lowercases the item side at comparison: effectiveAllergens.some(a => collisionSet.has(String(a).toLowerCase())). So customerAllergens ['GLUTEN'] vs item 'gluten' -> both 'gluten' -> match -> template :role="hasCollision ? 'alert' : 'group'" (line 8) renders role=alert + aria-live=assertive + --warning red frame. Confirmed by passing regression test tests/js/ksAllergenBadgeCollision.spec.js (GLUTEN -> hasCollision true; 'Poisson' absent from item -> false; lowercase exact still true) = 3/3 pass. Reverse direction (uppercase ITEM code) also covered since hasCollision and the per-item template highlight (line 19 collisionSet.has(String(code).toLowerCase())) both lowercase the item side too — fully symmetric.

(b) NO un-lowercased comparison path remains. effectiveAllergens (lines 95-104) comes either from mergeAllergens->extractAllergenCodes (kioskFilters.js:109-136, already lowercases all forms: string-split line 115, object code/name lines 121-124, flags line 133) OR from the raw allergens prop. In BOTH cases the three comparison sites — hasCollision (line 115), visibleAllergens compact filter (line 121), template item highlight (line 19) — apply String(...).toLowerCase() to the item code at comparison time. Display methods iconFor/localize use raw code but operate only on item catalog codes (already lowercase), not customer codes, so no display defect.

(c) FE-only is SUFFICIENT. Backend readDeclaredAllergens (LoyaltyController.php:1036-1054) only does array_map('strval',...) preserving case, and store SET_CUSTOMER_PROFILE (kioskSettings.js:223-224) only .map(String). Declared allergens flow verbatim to customerAllergenCodes (KioskWizardComponent.vue:544-545, KioskCartComponent.vue:472-473, KioskCategoriesComponent.vue:431) into the badge prop. Because every consumer lowercases at comparison (component collisionSet + helper getAllergenCollision kioskFilters.js:96), the verbatim backend case is harmless. Backend normalization would be defense-in-depth only, not a correctness requirement.

V1-LOCAL fence respected. KsAllergenBadge.vue and kioskFilters.js are NOT frozen zones (frozen kiosk files Wizard/App/Upsell only pass the prop through, unmodified).

new_p2_p3.title: normalizeAllergensForHash: heal #9 string-decode newly exposes array-of-objects snapshot to PHP 'Array to string conversion' warning (theoretical, no writer produces this shape)
new_p2_p3.evidence: Heal #9 added an is_string() decode branch (lines 600-606). Before the heal, any string-shaped allergens_snapshot returned [] (string -> not array -> []). After the heal, a string-encoded array-of-OBJECTS, e.g. json_encode([["code"=>"gluten"]]), now json_decodes to a nested array, then array_map('strval', ...) at line 613 hits each nested array element. Reproduced via php -r: input '[{"code":"gluten"}]' -> 'PHP Warning: Array to string conversion' and result ['Array']. CONFIRMED NOT REACHABLE: every writer stores a FLAT array of string codes — BackfillAllergensSnapshotCommand.php:94 json_encode($codes), OrderItemAllergenSnapshot.php:67 json_encode(...codes...), migration 2026_04_20_131600:51 json_encode($remapped) (remapped scalar codes). No code path writes array-of-objects. Also it only WARNS (array_map strval), never throws/fatals. Defensive-robustness only; introduced by heal #9.

new_p2_p3.title: Heal #15 abort(403) branch-guard is swallowed into HTTP 422 because forcePosRuntimeBranchScope() is called INSIDE lookupBarcode's try/catch(Exception)
new_p2_p3.file_line: app/Http/Controllers/Admin/ItemController.php:281 (call) inside try at :254, caught at :307; abort source forcePosRuntimeBranchScope():320
new_p2_p3.evidence: Heal #15 (commit 0cc50af95) changed lookupBarcode to call $this->forcePosRuntimeBranchScope($request) at line 281, which sits INSIDE the try{ } opened at line 254 and caught by catch(Exception $exception){ return response([...],422); } at line 307. forcePosRuntimeBranchScope():320 does abort_if($branchId < 1, 403). Confirmed via vendor: Illuminate\Foundation\Application::abort() (Application.php:1166) throws Symfony\Component\HttpKernel\Exception\HttpException for code 403; reflection on that class shows chain HttpException -> RuntimeException -> Exception (implements Throwable). Therefore the intended 403 is caught as \Exception and re-emitted as 422 with empty message. CONTRAST: the two pre-existing callers place the same call OUTSIDE their try — index() at :46 (try opens :98) and itemDetails() at :228 (try opens :242) — so their 403 propagates correctly. Only lookupBarcode (the heal) regresses the guard. Reachability: a staff account with 'pos' but not 'items_show' (POS Operator/Branch Manager per RolePermissionTableSeeder.php:96-110, branchManager :25-93) AND branch_id<1 (misconfig; V1-LOCAL seeds branch_id=1) scanning a barcode gets 422 instead of 403; frozen pos-app.js treats only 404 as null so a 422 hits its reject() path = uncontrolled error toast. Guard-degradation regression, low V1-LOCAL reachability.
